{{Short description|Czech mathematician and politician}}
'''Jaroslav Kožešník''' (8 June 1907 – 26 June 1985) was a Czech mathematician, scientist and politician. He was an expert in mechanics and automation ([[cybernetics]]) and worked as an editor-in-chief of the ''Kybernetika'' journal. He was a chairman of the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]] (1969–1970, 1970–1977, 1977–1980), a [[Communist Party of Czechoslovakia|Communist Party]] functionary in [[Czechoslovak Socialist Republic|Socialist Czechoslovakia]] and a member of the parliament during the [[Normalization (Czechoslovakia)|normalization]] period. He was a recipient of several state awards.<ref>{{cite web |title=Akad. Jaroslav Kožešník|url=https://www.psp.cz/sqw/detail.sqw?org=280&id=2263|publisher=[[Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic]]|language=cs|access-date=2026-04-10}}</ref><ref name=k60>"{{cite journal |title=K šedesátinám akademika Jaroslava Kožešníka|url=https://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/125262/Kybernetika_03-1967-3_1.pdf|journal=Kybernetika|volume=3|year=1967|issue=3|pages=219–222|language=cs}}</ref><ref name=obit>{{cite journal |title=Academik Jaroslav Kožešník 1907--1985|url=https://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/125452/Kybernetika_21-1985-4_1.pdf|journal=Kybernetika|volume=21|year=1985|issue=4|pages=249–250|language=cs}}</ref>

==Life==
Kožešník was born on 8 June 1907 in [[Kněžice (Jihlava District)|Kněžice]], Bohemia, Austria-Hungary. He died on 26 June 1985 in [[Prague]].

==Books==
*1983: ''Teorie podobnosti a modelování''<ref name=obit/>
*1979: ''Kmitání mechanických soustav''<ref name=obit/>
*1965: ''Základy teorie přístrojů'' (Principles of the Theory of Machines)<ref name=k60/>
*1960: ''Dynamika strojů'' (Dynamics of Machines), translated into English, German, Russian, Polish<ref name=k60/>
*1960: ''Mechanika elektrických strojů točivých'' (The Mechanics of Electrical Rotating Machines), translated into several languages<ref name=k60/>
*1947: ''Fysikální podobnost a stavba modelů''<ref name=obit/>

==Awards==
Honorary title of the Hero of Socialist Labor of Czechoslovak Socialist Republic, the Order of the Republic, the Order of the Victorious February, Order of Labour, A. Zápotockého medal with ribbon, the Soviet [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]], [[Order of Friendship of Peoples]] (awarded by the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union), Star friendship Nations in gold (awarded by the State Council of the GDR). For scientific merit is twice laureate of the Klement Gottwald State Prize, received the highest scientific honors the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union, [[Lomonosov Gold Medal]], two honorary gold plaques of the SCAS "For Merits of science and humanity" and a plaque of [[Zdeněk Nejedlý]].<ref name=obit/>
